descripcion_es: Unreal conditions in the past; past cause with present result and vice versa.
resumen: The third conditional imagines a different past and its consequence in the past (es: si hubiera… habría…). Mixed conditionals combine a past condition with a present result, or a present situation with a past result.

filas: If I had left earlier, I would have caught the train.
If I had taken the job, I would live in London now.
If I spoke French, I would have understood the guide.

explicacion.texto: The third conditional talks about something that did not happen: the condition and the result are both in the past and impossible to change. It is equivalent to Spanish “si hubiera hecho, habría hecho”.
Would never goes in the if clause: If I had known (not If I would have known). In speech, 'd can be had or would: If I'd known, I'd have told you.

items: Could have / might have in the result express possibility: If you had asked, I might have helped.
Formal inversion without if: Had I known, I would have told you (= If I had known).
But for + noun / If it hadn't been for + noun: “without”, “if it were not for” (es: “de no ser por”).
Clue for mixed conditionals: look at the time markers (now, today, yesterday, last year).

ejemplos.frase: If we had booked earlier, we would have got better seats.
ejemplos.traduccion: Si hubiéramos reservado antes, habríamos conseguido mejores asientos.

ejemplos.frase: She wouldn't have missed the flight if the taxi had arrived on time.
ejemplos.traduccion: No habría perdido el vuelo si el taxi hubiera llegado a tiempo.

ejemplos.frase: If I hadn't broken my leg, I would be playing in the final today.
ejemplos.traduccion: Si no me hubiera roto la pierna, hoy estaría jugando la final.

ejemplos.frase: If he were more careful, he wouldn't have crashed the car.
ejemplos.traduccion: Si fuera más cuidadoso, no habría estrellado el coche.

ejemplos.frase: Had the bank lowered rates sooner, the recession might have been shorter.
ejemplos.traduccion: Si el banco hubiera bajado los tipos antes, la recesión podría haber sido más corta.

ejemplos.frase: If it hadn't been for your help, I would never have finished the thesis.
ejemplos.traduccion: De no ser por tu ayuda, nunca habría terminado la tesis.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: If I would have known, I would have come.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: If I had known, I would have come.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The if clause uses had + past participle, never would.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: If I had studied medicine, I would have been a doctor now.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: With now the result is present: mixed conditional with would + infinitive.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: If you would have told me, I had helped you.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: If you had told me, I would have helped you.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The typical calque reverses the order: had goes with if and would have in the result.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form (third conditional).
ejercicios.frase: If she ___ (not / forget) her passport, she would have flown to Lisbon.
respuestas: hadn't forgotten
had not forgotten
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the first row of the table: in the third conditional the if clause is in the past perfect (had + past participle). The clue is the result, would have flown, which places everything in an unreal past: in reality, he forgot his passport and did not fly. The negative is formed with hadn't or had not + forgotten, the irregular past participle of forget; both forms are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The unreal past condition goes in the past perfect.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si no se hubiera olvidado el pasaporte, habría volado a Lisboa.

errores_previstos.respuesta: wouldn't have forgotten
errores_previstos.explicacion: Would never goes in the if clause; the condition goes in the past perfect: hadn't forgotten.

errores_previstos.respuesta: didn't forget
errores_previstos.explicacion: Past simple: it would be a second conditional and does not fit the result would have flown.

errores_previstos.respuesta: hadn't forgot
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past participle of forget is forgotten; forgot is the past simple.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form (third conditional).
ejercicios.frase: If you had asked me, I ___ (lend) you the money.
respuestas: would have lent
'd have lent
would've lent
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the third conditional table: the condition in the past perfect (had asked) requires would have + past participle in the result. The clue is had asked in the if clause. Lend is irregular (lend, lent, lent), so the past participle is lent. The contractions 'd have lent and would've lent are also accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The result of the third conditional is would have + past participle (lend → lent).
ejercicios.traduccion: Si me lo hubieras pedido, te habría prestado el dinero.

errores_previstos.respuesta: would have lend
errores_previstos.explicacion: After have comes the past participle: lent, not the infinitive lend.

errores_previstos.respuesta: would lend
errores_previstos.explicacion: Would + infinitive is a present result; with had asked and no now the result is past: would have lent.

errores_previstos.respuesta: would have lended
errores_previstos.explicacion: Lend is irregular: the past participle is lent.

ejercicios.frase: If I had saved more when I was young, I ___ (be) rich now.
respuestas: would be
'd be
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the past-to-present mixed conditional from the table: condition in the past perfect and result with would + infinitive. The decisive clue is now at the end: the consequence of not having saved is felt in the present. That is why we say would be, not would have been. The contraction 'd be is also accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Past cause with present result (now): would + infinitive.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si hubiera ahorrado más de joven, ahora sería rico.

errores_previstos.respuesta: would have been
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the typical error noted on the card: with now the result is present, would be.

errores_previstos.respuesta: will be
errores_previstos.explicacion: Will expresses a real result; here the situation is unreal: would be.

errores_previstos.respuesta: am
errores_previstos.explicacion: The present would indicate a fact, not a hypothesis; would be is needed.

ejercicios.frase: If he ___ (be) a better swimmer, he would have crossed the river easily.
respuestas: were
was
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the present-to-past mixed conditional from the table: past simple in the condition and would have + past participle in the result. The clue is that being a good swimmer is a permanent trait (he is not one, either now or before), whereas crossing the river was a specific event in the past. Were, the careful form for all persons, is accepted, and so is was, which is more colloquial.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Present, permanent trait (he is not a good swimmer) with past result: past simple in the condition.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si fuera mejor nadador, habría cruzado el río fácilmente.

errores_previstos.respuesta: had been
errores_previstos.explicacion: It would be understood as a one-off event in the past; the permanent trait is expressed with the past simple: were or was. The card presents this case as mixed.

errores_previstos.respuesta: would be
errores_previstos.explicacion: Would never goes in the if clause.

errores_previstos.respuesta: is
errores_previstos.explicacion: The present would indicate a real condition; here it is unreal: were or was.

ejercicios.frase: If they ___ the warning signs, the accident wouldn't have happened.
respuestas: had noticed
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule of the third conditional: if + past perfect, with the result would have + past participle. The clue is wouldn't have happened in the main clause, which requires a condition in the past perfect. The card insists that would never goes in the if clause.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si hubieran visto las señales de aviso, el accidente no habría ocurrido.

por_opcion.had noticed: Correct: past perfect in the condition of the third conditional.
por_opcion.would have noticed: Incorrect: it is the calque of Spanish “si habrían visto”; would does not go in the if clause.
por_opcion.noticed: Incorrect: the past simple belongs to the second conditional and does not fit wouldn't have happened.
por_opcion.have noticed: Incorrect: the present perfect is not used in unreal conditionals.

ejercicios.frase: If I hadn't missed the bus this morning, I ___ late for work now.
respuestas: wouldn't be
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the past-to-present mixed conditional and the card's clue for mixed conditionals: look at the time markers. This morning places the cause in the past and now requires a present result. That is why the result is wouldn't + infinitive: wouldn't be.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Past cause, present result (now): mixed conditional.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si no hubiera perdido el autobús esta mañana, ahora no llegaría tarde al trabajo.

por_opcion.wouldn't have been: Incorrect: it would be a past result, incompatible with now.
por_opcion.wouldn't be: Correct: present result of a past cause (mixed conditional).
por_opcion.won't be: Incorrect: will indicates something real and future; here the situation is hypothetical.

ejercicios.frase: ___ for the rain, we would have finished the match.
respuestas: If it hadn't been
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the structure from Rules and key points If it hadn't been for + noun, “without” (es: “de no ser por”), in the past. The clue is for the rain after the gap and the result would have finished, which places everything in the past. The subject it is compulsory, even though Spanish does not express it.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: If it hadn't been for = without (in the past) (es: de no ser por).
ejercicios.traduccion: De no haber sido por la lluvia, habríamos terminado el partido.

por_opcion.If it hadn't been: Correct: If it hadn't been for (es: de no haber sido por).
por_opcion.Had not been: Incorrect: formal inversion needs the subject it: Had it not been for the rain.
por_opcion.If it wasn't: Incorrect: it is the present version (If it wasn't for), which does not fit would have finished.
por_opcion.Unless it had been: Incorrect: unless is not combined with for in this structure and would change the meaning.

ejercicios.frase: If we would have left earlier, we would have avoided the traffic.
respuestas: If we had left earlier, we would have avoided the traffic.
If we'd left earlier, we would have avoided the traffic.
If we had left earlier, we'd have avoided the traffic.
If we had left earlier, we would've avoided the traffic.
If we'd left earlier, we'd have avoided the traffic.
If we'd left earlier, we would've avoided the traffic.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule from Rules and key points: would never goes in the if clause. The original sentence repeats would have in both parts, which is the calque of colloquial Spanish “si habríamos salido”. The condition must be in the past perfect: had left (or 'd left). All combinations with contractions are accepted (we'd left, we'd have, would've).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Would is not used in the if clause.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si hubiéramos salido antes, habríamos evitado el tráfico.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If we would have left earlier, we would have avoided the traffic.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: would does not go in the if clause.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If we left earlier, we would have avoided the traffic.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The unreal past condition goes in the past perfect, had left, not in the past simple.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If we had left earlier, we had avoided the traffic.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Calque of Spanish “hubiéramos evitado”: the result takes would have.

ejercicios.frase: If I had accepted that offer, I would have lived in Canada now.
respuestas: If I had accepted that offer, I would live in Canada now.
If I had accepted that offer, I'd live in Canada now.
If I'd accepted that offer, I would live in Canada now.
If I'd accepted that offer, I'd live in Canada now.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the past-to-present mixed conditional and the typical error noted on the card: with now the result is present. The condition (had accepted) is past, but the consequence is lived now, so it takes would + infinitive: would live. All combinations with contractions are accepted (I'd accepted, I'd live).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With now the result is present: would + infinitive.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si hubiera aceptado aquella oferta, ahora viviría en Canadá.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If I had accepted that offer, I would have lived in Canada now.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: would have lived is past and clashes with now.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If I would have accepted that offer, I would live in Canada now.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It introduces a new mistake: would cannot go in the if clause.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If I had accepted that offer, I will live in Canada now.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Will expresses something real; for a hypothetical result we use would live.

ejercicios.frase: If she had studied harder, she would pass the exam last June.
respuestas: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam last June.
If she had studied harder, she'd have passed the exam last June.
If she had studied harder, she would've passed the exam last June.
If she'd studied harder, she would have passed the exam last June.
If she'd studied harder, she'd have passed the exam last June.
If she'd studied harder, she would've passed the exam last June.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the full third conditional: condition and result in the past. The clue is last June, which places the result in the past. The original sentence uses would pass, typical of a present result, which does not fit that time marker; would have + past participle is needed: would have passed. All combinations with contractions are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The result refers to the past (last June): would have + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si hubiera estudiado más, habría aprobado el examen el pasado junio.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If she had studied harder, she would pass the exam last June.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: with last June the result is past, would have passed.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If she had studied harder, she would have pass the exam last June.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After have comes the past participle: passed.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If she would have studied harder, she would have passed the exam last June.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It corrects the result but puts would in the if clause, which never takes would.

ejercicios.enunciado: Join the ideas in one third conditional sentence beginning with If.
ejercicios.frase: I didn't know you were ill, so I didn't visit you.
respuestas: If I had known you were ill, I would have visited you.
If I'd known you were ill, I would have visited you.
If I had known you were ill, I'd have visited you.
If I'd known you were ill, I'd have visited you.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the third conditional: two real, negative facts in the past (I didn't know, I didn't visit you) become an affirmative hypothesis. The condition goes in the past perfect (had known) and the result in would have + past participle (would have visited). The clause you were ill does not change. All combinations of contractions are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The two negative realities are turned into affirmative hypotheses.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si hubiera sabido que estabas enfermo, te habría visitado.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If I knew you were ill, I would have visited you.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The condition is also past: had known, not knew.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If I would have known you were ill, I would have visited you.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Would does not go in the if clause: had known.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If I hadn't known you were ill, I wouldn't have visited you.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It keeps the negatives and almost describes reality; they must be turned into affirmatives.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence with inversion, without if.
ejercicios.frase: If I had known about the strike, I would have taken the car.
respuestas: Had I known about the strike, I would have taken the car.
Had I known about the strike, I'd have taken the car.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the formal inversion without if from Rules and key points: had moves in front of the subject and if disappears. “Had I known” is equivalent to “If I had known” and belongs to the formal or written register. The result does not change. The contraction I'd have is also accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: In a formal register, had moves in front of the subject and if disappears.
ejercicios.traduccion: De haber sabido lo de la huelga, habría cogido el coche.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If had I known about the strike, I would have taken the car.
errores_previstos.explicacion: With inversion, if disappears: Had I known.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I had known about the strike, I would have taken the car.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Without if and without inversion it is a statement, not a condition; had must go in front of the subject.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Had I knew about the strike, I would have taken the car.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After had comes the past participle: known.

ejercicios.enunciado: Join the ideas in a mixed conditional beginning with If.
ejercicios.frase: He didn't take the medicine, so he is ill now.
respuestas: If he had taken the medicine, he wouldn't be ill now.
If he had taken the medicine, he would not be ill now.
If he'd taken the medicine, he wouldn't be ill now.
If he'd taken the medicine, he would not be ill now.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the past-to-present mixed conditional. The cause is past (he didn't take the medicine) and the effect is present (he is ill now). That is why the condition goes in the past perfect (had taken) and the result in would + infinitive, in the negative: wouldn't be ill now. Both realities are reversed. All combinations with contractions are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Past cause (past perfect) and present result (would + infinitive).
ejercicios.traduccion: Si se hubiera tomado la medicina, ahora no estaría enfermo.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If he had taken the medicine, he wouldn't have been ill now.
errores_previstos.explicacion: With now the result is present: wouldn't be.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If he took the medicine, he wouldn't be ill now.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The condition is a past fact: had taken.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If he had taken the medicine, he would be ill now.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The result has not been reversed: if he had taken it, he would not be ill now.

respuestas: if you had called I would have come
I would have come if you had called
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the structure of the third conditional: if + past perfect (had called) and would have + past participle (would have come). Both orders are accepted because the if clause can go before or after the main clause. Come has a past participle identical to the infinitive: come.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si me hubieras llamado, habría venido. (También: Habría venido si me hubieras llamado.)

errores_previstos.respuesta: if you would have called I had come
errores_previstos.explicacion: It swaps the tenses, the typical calque the card points out: had goes with if and would have in the result.

errores_previstos.respuesta: if had you called I would have come
errores_previstos.explicacion: It mixes if with inversion; either if you had called or had you called (without if).

respuestas: they might have won the game
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the note from Rules and key points: could have or might have in the result express possibility, not certainty. Might have + past participle indicates that winning was possible, but not certain. The order is subject + might + have + past participle (won) + complement.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Might have + past participle expresses a possible, not certain, result.

errores_previstos.respuesta: they might won have the game
errores_previstos.explicacion: After might comes have and then the past participle: might have won.

errores_previstos.respuesta: they have might won the game
errores_previstos.explicacion: The modal goes first: might have, not have might.

descripcion_larga_es: The third conditional imagines a past different from the real one and its consequence, also in the past (“if I had left earlier, I would have caught the train”). Mixed conditionals cross the tenses: a past condition with a present result, or the other way round. They are used to express regret, to reproach and to analyse decisions. They are difficult for Spanish speakers because the calque of “si habría” leads them to put would in the if clause.

contexto.que_es: The third conditional joins an unreal condition in the past (if + had + past participle) with a result that is also past and impossible (would/could/might have + past participle). Mixed conditionals combine that past condition with a present result (would + infinitive), or a permanent present situation (past simple) with a past result (would have + past participle).
contexto.por_que_importa: It is the tool for talking about what might have been: regrets, reproaches, analysis of mistakes and of economic policy decisions (“if interest rates had been raised earlier…”). Mixing the tenses badly produces ungrammatical sentences or confusion about when each thing happens. In B2 and C1 exams it is a classic point, especially the error of would in the if clause.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When talking about past events that can no longer be changed and imagining an alternative. The signals are the time markers: yesterday, last June or this morning for the past; now or today for a present result, which requires a mixed conditional. Spanish speakers tend to write If I would have… because of the calque of “si habría”, and to use would have with now.
